## Disposition and exact scope

Accepted scoped partial results for 30001092 / OWR-2487-003. The full source target remains unresolved by this work at 5/5 substantive approaches. No sixth construction route, substantive mathematical correction, novelty claim, exhaustive-priority claim or present-day-openness claim. No QUEUE change.

The exact question asks for two essentially free p.m.p. actions of one countable group on standard atomless probability spaces, one with an FI orbit relation and one without. There is no global ergodicity hypothesis. The literal catalogue omission of freeness is not used to broaden the category.

## Accepted mathematics and boundaries

Read the unchanged complete authored/SCOPED_RESULTS.md, audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md and audit/CONTEXTUAL_SUPPLEMENT.md, together with authored/EXACT_STATEMENT_AND_SOURCES.md and audit/SCOPE_ACCEPTANCE.md. All 11 authored files and the separate public audit seal are preserved byte-for-byte. The independent review found no substantive defect. The supplement clarifies existing arguments and source attribution without changing any frozen conclusion or hypothesis.

- The quotient construction is a nonfree false positive; taking a diagonal product repairs freeness but destroys its FI certificate.
- Inessentiality uses a Borel complete section partitioned into invariant pieces with equality of the restricted relations, modulo invariant null sets. Completeness need not mean full measure; invariant slicings and smooth connectors remain inessential.
- The canonical infinite-factor-support criterion, recurrence and countable-mixture result retain their aperiodic p.m.p. hypotheses. Non-FI ergodic extraction disintegrates one fixed splitting. No selection among varying decompositions, nor FI-almost-every-ergodic-component converse, is asserted.
- The locally orbit-bijective direction is FI extension implies FI factor. Its contrapositive gives non-FI factor implies non-FI extension. No blanket upward FI transfer or common-product ergodicity is asserted.
- Finite-index induction and finite-normal-quotient reduction retain their stated directions. Reverse transport is proved for a split finite direct factor only. These operations require a seed; infinite-index counting induction is not a probability action.
- The conditional Z-cocycle FI theorem requires a countable nonamenable group Gamma, Hom(Gamma,Z)=0, a free ergodic p.m.p. action on a standard atomless probability space, and superrigidity for every measurable Z-cocycle of that action. It supplies no mixed pair.
- TW arXiv:2410.11754v3 Lemma 5.1 requires ergodicity and supplies a full-domain aperiodic amenable free factor. Connes–Feldman–Weiss supplies its generator without requiring factor ergodicity. The full-domain generator, measurable free-product cocycle extension and probability-level-set contradiction retain their exact assumptions.
- The Peterson–Sinclair obstruction is to the stronger U_fin-superrigid Bernoulli route, not Z-only superrigidity for arbitrary actions. The strong-treeability exclusions require essential freeness, aperiodicity and the cited essential-decomposition theorem; ordinary group indecomposability is insufficient.

The full target is neither solved by a verified mixed pair nor excluded by a general impossibility theorem. Mathematical acceptance rests on the authored arguments and independent audit relative to their explicitly stated imported interfaces. No mathematical computation or sampled-orbit certificate is claimed. Full proofs of all source papers and foundations were not independently reproved.

Public sources include Alvarez–Gaboriau, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/29614; OWR 49/2008, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46193; Tucker-Drob–Wróbel v3, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11754v3; Conley–Gaboriau–Marks–Tucker-Drob v3, https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07431v3; Peterson–Sinclair, https://math.vanderbilt.edu/peters10/petersonsinclair.pdf; and Connes–Feldman–Weiss, https://doi.org/10.1017/S014338570000136X.

## Historical evidence and publication-stage controls

Historical source versions, public PDF byte counts/hashes, retrieval history and selected text/page inspections are preserved metadata. They are not fresh publication-stage source downloads or source-body replays, nor cryptographic authentication of historical network provenance. PDF-header detection is not digital-signature verification. Original audit statements that no code execution or publication was performed remain true descriptions of that stage. The separate new publication software validates documents, declarations and delivery integrity only.

Every publication-mode run verifies 12 preserved document/seal byte identities and two exact scope declarations. These are document controls, not proof-check counts. Separately, 46 integrity rejections, 63 schema/scope rejections, 32 complete-output comparator rejections and 33 physical create/append-open/unlink denials pass per mode. All control identities, counts and intended rejection reasons are fixed and checked. Empty, malformed, changed, skipped, expected-failure, missing-identity, altered-count and wrong-mode outputs fail closed. Full raw stdout/stderr bytes and recursive exact JSON types match their mode-specific references; hostile environment/current-directory imports match the complete baseline, and all packet hashes remain unchanged.

Fresh normal/-O/-OO runs used -I -S -B with actual UID=EUID=1000. A separately reconstructed packet from the exact additive diff was rerun under all three modes; its complete raw stdout/stderr and recursively typed results matched the initial final controls exactly. The trusted runtime and standard library remain assumptions; read-only modes protect against accidental writes, not root or deliberate owner chmod.

Source-body, historical retrieval/inspection, excluded-material, new-source-search, dataset, full foundational proof, formal proof assistant, computational mathematical certification, publisher-PDF comparison and cryptographic PDF-signature verification are NOT_RUN. Only authored mathematics/audit/supplement, acceptance, safe verification code, public source metadata and verification receipts are included. No source PDFs/text/images, datasets, private sources, private personal or coordination material, or identifying metadata for excluded private material are included.

## Public reproduction and external trust

Authenticate BOOTSTRAP.py against the independently reviewed SHA-256 below before executing it. Copy that authenticated file outside the packet. Set packet files to 0444 and directories to 0555, then use actual UID=EUID=1000:

- python -I -S -B /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet
- python -I -S -B -O /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet
- python -I -S -B -OO /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet

The external bootstrap binds the manifest, verifier and rejection harness. The manifest binds every other delivered byte, including the complete accepted documents, public audit seal, declarations, code, pre-seal receipt and full raw stdout/stderr references. It excludes only itself and BOOTSTRAP.py, whose hashes are bound outward. Final receipts remain outside the bound inventory to avoid circular hashes and are pinned below. Do not choose a new trust anchor by hashing an untrusted download; use the independently reviewed value. Identical mode-specific raw output digests below give an external reproduction comparison.
